analysis.subject: earth-science
analysis.pageCoverage: This source explains the continuous circulation of water between ground and atmosphere and describes evaporation transpiration condensation precipitation and runoff with energy dew point and salty lake examples.

overview.headline: Water moves continuously between earth and atmosphere

keyPoints.point: Students learn that evaporation is the change of state from liquid to gas and requires energy.
keyPoints.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that transpiration is evaporation of water from plants through stomata into the atmosphere.
keyPoints.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that condensation is the process where water vapor changes into liquid and releases heat.
keyPoints.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that precipitation can be rain hail snow or sleet formed when particles grow too large.
keyPoints.quote: Precipitation can be in the form of rain, hail, snow, or sleet.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that runoff occurs when excessive precipitation leaves the ground saturated and water cannot absorb more.
keyPoints.quote: Runoff occurs when there is excessive precipitation and the ground is saturated (cannot absorb any more water).

keyTerms.gloss: change of liquid to vapor that needs energy to take place
keyTerms.quote: For evaporation to take place, energy is required.

keyTerms.gloss: evaporation of water from plants through leaf openings into the air
keyTerms.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyTerms.gloss: process where water vapor changes into liquid and releases heat
keyTerms.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyTerms.gloss: falling water in the form of rain snow hail or sleet
keyTerms.quote: Precipitation can be in the form of rain, hail, snow, or sleet.

keyTerms.gloss: water that flows over saturated ground into rivers and lakes
keyTerms.quote: Runoff occurs when there is excessive precipitation and the ground is saturated (cannot absorb any more water).

keyTerms.gloss: temperature where air becomes saturated and foggy conditions can occur
keyTerms.quote: Foggy conditions often occur when air temperature and dew point are equal.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: The cycle is taught as an ordered circulation where each process feeds the next so sequencing builds understanding of cause and flow.
componentPlan.focusQuote: The hydrologic cycle involves the continuous circulation of water in the Earth-Atmosphere system.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: The figure shows the whole system in one view and labeling helps connect names to movements between earth and sky.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Rivers and lakes are results of runoff.
